title: Contract Year 2026 Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines
cfr_reference: 42 CFR Part 422 Subpart V; 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart V
notes_on_extraction: Use the current-contract-year TPMO disclaimer, prohibited-content, marketing conduct, and required-material timing sections. Treat this as operational CMS guidance that interprets the governing CFR provisions and should be read alongside 42 CFR 422 Subpart V.
rule_excerpt: Current CMS marketing guidance should be used for TPMO disclaimer content, required materials timing, prohibited or misleading marketing conduct, and star-ratings use. This source is operationally central but remains subordinate to current statute and regulation if a conflict appears.

title: 42 CFR Part 422 Subpart V - Communications and Marketing
notes_on_extraction: Part-level controlling regulation for MA communications and marketing. Use the subpart for section crosswalks, especially required content, marketing definitions, plan website and material obligations, and conduct restrictions.
rule_excerpt: This subpart is the controlling MA marketing regulation set. Use it as the primary authority for required content, communications definitions, marketing standards, and conduct controls; CMS guidance and carrier workflows should not override it.

title: 42 CFR 422.2267 - Required Content
notes_on_extraction: Use subsection references for required materials and content controls, including TPMO disclaimer obligations and timing/content obligations attached to standardized and marketing materials.
rule_excerpt: This section governs required content in MA communications and marketing materials. It is the key citation for TPMO disclaimer obligations and other required material content rules that later CMS guidance operationalizes.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Contract Year 2026 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage Program, Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program, Medicare Cost Plan Program, and Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly
notes_on_extraction: Current-cycle final rule affecting CY 2026 operations. Use for identifying codified changes, new regulatory text, and whether prior subregulatory guidance has been superseded or codified. Treat as current rulemaking authority over older CMS guidance where applicable.
rule_excerpt: The CY 2026 final rule revises Medicare Advantage and Part D regulations and codifies certain subregulatory guidance. Use it to check whether earlier marketing or SNP guidance has been superseded by current regulatory text applicable to coverage beginning January 1, 2026.

title: Medicare Program; Changes to the Medicare Advantage and the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program for Contract Year 2024—Remaining Provisions and Contract Year 2025 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage Program, Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program, Medicare Cost Plan Program, and Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE)
notes_on_extraction: Retain for historical traceability and audit comparison only. Compare against CY 2026 final rule and current CFR before relying on any marketing or SNP language.
rule_excerpt: This rule remains useful for historical change tracking, but compliance enforcement should treat later contract-year rulemaking and the current eCFR text as controlling where the provisions differ.

title: Joining a Plan
notes_on_extraction: Use the eligibility and timing table. This page is especially useful for operationalizing Part A/Part B requirements, service area rules, lawfully present status, and high-level effective-date logic.
rule_excerpt: To join a Medicare Advantage plan, a person generally must have Part A and Part B, live in the plan’s service area, be a U.S. citizen or lawfully present, and enroll during a valid enrollment period. Effective dates depend on the election period and when the request is received.

title: Open Enrollment
notes_on_extraction: Use for AEP timing, available plan changes, and January 1 effective-date logic for valid requests received by December 7.
rule_excerpt: Open Enrollment runs from October 15 through December 7. Changes made during that period are effective January 1 of the next year if the plan receives the enrollment request by December 7.

title: Special Enrollment Periods
notes_on_extraction: Use the life-event matrix for move, Medicaid loss, employer/union loss, LIS/Medicaid monthly flexibility, integrated D-SNP monthly SEP, C-SNP access, institutional status, incarceration release, plan non-renewal, low-performing plan, 5-star, and exceptional-circumstances timing.
rule_excerpt: SEP rights depend on the triggering event and the timing window. Medicare.gov provides an operational matrix for what plan changes are allowed and when they can be made for moves, loss of coverage, Medicaid or Extra Help status, SNP eligibility, institutional status, and other special situations.

title: When does Medicare coverage start?
notes_on_extraction: Use for Part A/Part B effective-date logic in special situations, including Medicaid-loss SEP and other delayed-enrollment timing. This is useful for validating whether plan effective dates are being overstated.
rule_excerpt: Coverage-start timing depends on how and when Medicare entitlement is established. In special enrollment situations, Medicare.gov explains when Part B starts and how that timing affects when later MA or Part D enrollment can validly begin.

title: CMS Center for Medicare: NAIC Q&A and Follow-Ups
notes_on_extraction: Use Question 22 for outbound enrollment verification and the network-change Q&A for CMS discussion of significant provider-network change SEP logic. This is not the top-level authority but is still official CMS interpretive guidance.
rule_excerpt: CMS states MA organizations and Part D sponsors must maintain systems confirming that enrolled beneficiaries actually enrolled and understand plan rules. CMS also notes the MCMG expects outbound verification for agent or broker-assisted enrollments within 15 calendar days after receipt of the enrollment request.

title: Medicare Part B Giveback Benefit explained
notes_on_extraction: Operational-only carrier explanation. Use for workflow wording around how a giveback is applied through Social Security or reduced Medicare premium billing and the warning that processing may take a few months. Do not treat as regulatory authority.
rule_excerpt: Humana explains that a Part B giveback is a premium reduction, not a direct check from the plan. If the beneficiary pays Part B through Social Security, the reduction is credited there; otherwise Medicare billing is reduced. Processing may take a few months after plan enrollment.

title: UnitedHealthcare Group Medicare Quick Start Guide / Plan Guide
notes_on_extraction: Public carrier enrollment guide. Use only for operational expectations about post-approval mailing sequence, ID-card timing, and member onboarding. This is employer-group-specific and should not be generalized beyond workflow heuristics.
rule_excerpt: The guide states UnitedHealthcare will process enrollment, then mail a Quick Start Guide and member ID card 7 to 10 days after enrollment is approved. It also describes a health assessment outreach within the first 90 days after the plan effective date.

title: Wellcare Medicare Providers - ID Card Effective Date Guidance reference
notes_on_extraction: Provider-facing carrier page exposing a public document called 'Wellcare Medicare ID Card Effective Date Guidance.' Use only to support ID-card and effective-date workflow validation after manual review of the linked document.
rule_excerpt: The public provider resource page indicates Wellcare publishes plan operational guidance about the effective date shown on Medicare member ID cards. Use only as secondary workflow support after manual review of the underlying guidance document.
